questions.q: What happens the moment FBDI data is uploaded and loaded — does it immediately become a live record in the application (a real supplier, a real journal)?
options: Yes, uploading the file immediately creates the live record
No — it first lands in a staging area called an interface table, and only becomes a real record after a separate import process accepts it
No — FBDI never actually creates real records, only reports
Yes, but only on weekends
questions.explain: FBDI always stages data in interface tables first. A second, separate import process validates and promotes accepted rows into the real application tables.

questions.q: What are the three building blocks every FBDI load uses?
options: A password, a username, and a browser
A template, an interface table, and an import process
A printer, a scanner, and a fax machine
A REST API, a webhook, and a token
questions.explain: Every FBDI load follows the same pattern: a template maps to an interface table, and an import process moves validated rows from there into application tables.

questions.q: Why wasn't FBDI needed if Oracle Fusion already has transaction pages like Manage Suppliers or Create Journal?
options: Because those pages are built for one record at a time with real-time validation, and cannot practically absorb thousands of rows
Because those pages are broken and unusable
Because Oracle wanted to charge extra for a second tool
Because transaction pages don't exist in Oracle Fusion
questions.explain: Transaction pages are designed for single-record entry. FBDI exists so the same volume of data can pass through the same validation rules, just in bulk.

questions.q: Which scenario is the BEST fit for FBDI?
options: Posting five journal lines this afternoon
Converting 40,000 legacy supplier records into Oracle Fusion at go-live
A live, second-by-second feed with no file ever produced
Looking up one invoice's status
questions.explain: Large one-time conversions, like a legacy data migration at go-live, are exactly the volume FBDI's template-and-import pipeline is built for.

questions.q: Which scenario is the WRONG fit for FBDI, and better handled by a REST API integration instead?
options: A one-time supplier conversion at go-live
A monthly file of thousands of receivables transactions
A live, continuous, system-to-system feed running every few minutes with no file to produce
A large recurring scheduled batch load
questions.explain: FBDI depends on a file being produced and uploaded. A continuous, unattended feed with no file step is a REST API integration job, covered in the next course.
